Declare an inquiry

Source: R/declare_inquiry.R
declare_inquiry.Rd

Each named argument records an inquiry: an expression evaluated on the data as it stands when the step runs. Its value on a given draw is the estimand.

Usage

declare_inquiry(
  ...,
  subset = NULL,
  label = "inquiry",
  handler = NULL,
  draws = 1L
)

declare_inquiries(
  ...,
  subset = NULL,
  label = "inquiry",
  handler = NULL,
  draws = 1L
)

declare_estimand(
  ...,
  subset = NULL,
  label = "inquiry",
  handler = NULL,
  draws = 1L
)

declare_estimands(
  ...,
  subset = NULL,
  label = "inquiry",
  handler = NULL,
  draws = 1L
)

Arguments

...

(optional) Named expressions. Each expression becomes an inquiry whose numeric value is recorded in the simulation output. An unnamed expression takes the step's label as its name.

subset

(optional) Unquoted expression evaluated on the data; only rows where it is TRUE enter the estimands.

label

(optional) Step label. Defaults to "inquiry". A step that declares exactly one named inquiry takes that name as its label instead, overriding label.

handler

(optional) A function. When supplied, ... arguments are evaluated against the data and passed to handler() rather than being treated as named scalar inquiries; useful for vectorised inquiry sets (for example, handler = tibble).

draws

(optional) Number of nested draws for this step. Defaults to 1. When > 1, the step is re-executed draws times for each upstream draw during nested simulation.

Value

A design_step (class c("design_step", "dd", "function")): a function that takes a data frame and returns a tibble with columns inquiry and estimand, one row per inquiry. Add it to a design with +.

See also

Other design declarations: declare_assignment(), declare_estimator(), declare_measurement(), declare_model(), declare_notes(), declare_parameters(), declare_sampling(), declare_step(), declare_test()

Examples

design <-
  declare_model(N = 100, U = rnorm(N), Y_Z_0 = U, Y_Z_1 = U + 0.5) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0))

draw_estimands(design)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   inquiry estimand
#>   <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 ATE          0.5

# Placed before declare_sampling(), the question is about the population;
# placed after, about the sample.
design <-
  declare_model(N = 500, Y = rnorm(N)) +
  declare_inquiry(population_mean = mean(Y)) +
  declare_sampling(S = sample(rep(0:1, length.out = N))) +
  declare_inquiry(sample_mean = mean(Y))

draw_estimands(design)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   inquiry         estimand
#>   <chr>              <dbl>
#> 1 population_mean -0.00338
#> 2 sample_mean     -0.00732
